2607.18566.title: The Story Shapes the Agent: Narrative Priors in LLM Behavior
2607.18566.paper_summary: Persona prompting is widely used to steer LLM agent behavior, yet the narrative framing of a task can matter more than the assigned persona. We isolate this effect through structural isomorphism, constructing three text-based investigation games that share the same action space, stage progression, and resource constraints while varying only task narrative: disease investigation, IT troubleshooting, and murder mystery. Across 1,890 sessions spanning 3 models and 10 personas, we identify narrative priors: systematic action tendencies activated by a task's story framing, independent of its decision structure. Narrative priors explain 5-31x more behavioral variance than persona, are consistent across model architectures, and in two of three domains are negatively associated with task success. Persona effects that do transfer across narratives arise from behavioral anchors, persona descriptions whose language maps directly onto shared actions. Causal interventions confirm this: removing anchor words from a high-transfer persona reduces cross-narrative consistency by 95%. Our framework also generalizes to a held-out fourth narrative and yields a persona-selection method that improves cross-narrative transfer. These results suggest that LLM behavior that survives narrative changes should be grounded in concrete actions rather than abstract descriptions.
2607.18566.paper_summary_zh: Persona 提示被廣泛用來引導 LLM 代理的行為，然而，任務的敘事框架可能比指定的角色更為重要。<lb/>我們通過結構同構來孤立這一效應，構建了三個基於文本的調查遊戲，這些遊戲共享相同的行動空間、階段進展和資源限制，同時僅在任務敘事上有所不同：疾病調查、IT 故障排除和謀殺懸疑。<lb/>在涵蓋 3 種模型和 10 種角色的 1,890 次會話中，我們識別出敘事先驗：由任務的故事框架激活的系統性行動傾向，與其決策結構無關。<lb/>敘事先驗解釋了比角色多 5-31 倍的行為變異，並且在模型架構中保持一致，在三個領域中的兩個與任務成功呈負相關。<lb/>跨敘事轉移的角色效應來自行為錨點，即其語言直接映射到共享行動的角色描述。<lb/>因果干預證實了這一點：從高轉移角色中移除錨點詞語會將跨敘事一致性降低 95%。<lb/>我們的框架還可以推廣到一個保留的第四個敘事，並產生一種角色選擇方法，改善跨敘事轉移。<lb/>這些結果表明，能夠在敘事變化中存活的 LLM 行為應該基於具體行動，而非抽象描述。
